title: Classical torsion cohomology bound on proper weakly contractible neighborhoods
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $e\geq0$ be an integer bounding the Krull dimensions of all fibres of every base change of $f$ [def-pc-base-change] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $V\to Y$ be an affine weakly contractible object of the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible], put $Z=X\times_YV$, and let $h:Z\to V$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use ordinary module sheaves over the constant ring $A$, their total K-injective derived direct images and derived sections [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every classical $A$-module sheaf $H$ on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$, meaning $H\cong\nu_Z^*F$ for an étale $A$-module sheaf $F$ [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], one has
$$\mathcal H^qRh_*(H[0])=0,\qquad H^qR\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},H[0])=0\qquad(q>2e).$$
The assertion ranges over all classical sheaves on $Z$, including ones that do not descend from $X$. No Noetherianity of $V$, constructibility of $H$, or invertibility of the additive exponent of $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Base change of the proper morphism $f$ along $V\to Y$ is proper, so $h:Z\to V$ is proper. The assumed bound applies in particular to every fibre of $h$, with the same integer $e$. Properness includes finite type and separatedness. Finite type includes quasi-compactness, and separatedness implies quasi-separatedness; hence $h$ satisfies the qcqs hypothesis of the comparison theorem.

source.place: Tag 01W4, lemma-base-change-proper; Tag 01KK, definition-separated, and Tag 01K7, lemma-closed-immersion-quasi-compact

proof.text: Since $A$ is finite and discrete, the two finite-discrete coefficient lemmas identify, for $T=Z,V$, the coefficient ring sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] used in the statement with the constant ring sheaf $\nu_T^*A_{T,\mathrm{\acute et}}$, as rings. Hence the classical-module equivalence and the comparison statements for constant coefficients used below apply to the module sheaves of the statement. Choose an étale $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $Z$ with $H\cong\nu_Z^*F$, using the classical module equivalence. Since $A$ is finite, the additive order $n$ of $1_A$ is a positive integer and $n\cdot m=(n1_A)m=0$ for every local section $m$ of $F$. Thus its underlying abelian sheaf $U_ZF$ is torsion. For the zero ring take $n=1$; then $F=0$. This choice is made on $Z$ itself and imposes no descent condition from $X$.

source.place: Definition 5.1.3 and Lemma 5.1.2, module form; elementary finite-ring torsion argument

proof.text: Apply the proper torsion direct-image bound to $h$ and $U_ZF$: $R^qh_{\mathrm{ét},*}(U_ZF)=0$ for $q>2e$. The coefficient-forgetting comparison identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qh_{\mathrm{ét},*}F$ with this sheaf. Forgetting is faithful and detects zero, since a module with zero underlying abelian group is zero. Consequently $R^qh_{\mathrm{ét},*}F=0$. An ordinary bounded-below injective resolution of $F$ is K-injective, and computes both the total derived functor on $F[0]$ and its classical higher derived functors. Hence $\mathcal H^qRh_{\mathrm{ét},*}(F[0])=0$ for $q>2e$.

proof.text:
The complex $F[0]$ is bounded below, so the canonical total-derived comparison is invertible for the qcqs morphism $h$: $
u_V^*Rh_{\mathrm{ét},*}(F[0])\cong Rh_*(
u_Z^*F[0])\cong Rh_*(H[0])$. Here the bounded-below total-comparison node supplies precisely the compatibility with K-injective total derivation. The module comparison inverse image $
u_V^*$ is exact. An exact functor preserves kernels and images, hence the kernel/image quotient defining cohomology; therefore $\mathcal H^qRh_*(H[0])\cong
u_V^*\mathcal H^qRh_{\mathrm{ét},*}(F[0])=0$ for $q>2e$.

source.place: Transfer paragraph, bounded-below application; canonical mate and total D+ compatibility from sk-prop-pe-unbounded-classical-direct-image

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $H\to I^\bullet$ in the module-sheaf category. It is K-injective, so $h_*I^\bullet$ represents $Rh_*(H[0])$ and $\Gamma(Z,I^\bullet)$ represents $R\Gamma(Z,H[0])$. By the direct-image section formula, $\Gamma(Z,I^\bullet)=\Gamma(V,h_*I^\bullet)$ term by term. The weakly étale localization node identifies $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}/V$ and identifies the constant coefficient rings. We check that the final object $V$ of $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is weakly contractible there. Let $\varphi:F\to G$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets on $V_{\mathrm{proét}}=Y_{\mathrm{proét}}/V$ and $s\in G(V)$. For an object $U$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$ let $P(U)$ be the set of pairs $(a,t)$ with $a:U\to V$ a $Y$-morphism and $t\in F(U\xrightarrow{a}V)$ such that $\varphi(t)=s|_a$. Then $P$ is a sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$: for a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$, compatible $a_i$ glue to a unique $a$ because $h_V$ is a sheaf (the topology is subcanonical); the $t_i$ then glue in $F$ because the slice coverings are the coverings of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$; and $\varphi(t)=s|_a$ holds because $G$ is separated. The map $P\to h_V$, $(a,t)\mapsto a$, is an epimorphism: $\varphi$ is locally surjective, so $s|_a$ lifts on a covering of $U$. Since $V$ is weakly contractible in $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, this map has a section $\sigma$. Then $\sigma(\mathrm{id}_V)=(\mathrm{id}_V,t)$ with $t\in F(V)$ and $\varphi(t)=s$. Thus $V$ is a weakly contractible affine object of $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Exact evaluation applied there makes $\Gamma(V,-)$ exact on module sheaves of $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Exactness preserves the kernel/image quotients of the complex, giving $H^qR\Gamma(Z,H[0])=\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^qRh_*(H[0]))=0$ for $q>2e$.
